description: Compatibility traps, inherited build to build so they are recorded rather than rediscovered (REQ-VER-05). B16 applies every rule here after reading crates.io and before finalising versions/manifest.json. A trap is superseded with a reason, never deleted on a hunch.

traps.rule: Pair the two versions deliberately; do not bump one alone.
traps.why: A mismatched pair compiles and then disagrees about type layout. The failure is a memory bug at runtime, not a compile error, which makes it expensive to find.

traps.rule: A major bump is a reviewed decision with a migration note (REQ-VER-04).
traps.why: The crate moves fast and a major can rename types across every call site. The blast radius is bounded to crates/ffi on purpose (REQ-FND-03) - that is the payoff for the single-FFI-crate rule.

traps.rule: The minor versions must match exactly.
traps.why: A mismatch surfaces as a trait-resolution error deep in generic code rather than a version conflict, and reads like a code bug.

traps.rule: Its defaults do not satisfy REQ-UPD-02. Signature verification is ours to add.
traps.why: Adopting a crate because its name matches the requirement is how an unverified updater ships. If it is used at all, record what it does and does not do.

traps.rule: A dependency bump must not raise the MSRV above the pinned toolchain (REQ-VER-06).
traps.why: MSRV creep is silent until a contributor or a CI image with an older toolchain fails. CI tests the MSRV so it fails at the bump instead.
crates.io rejects a request without one, and the rejection reads like a missing crate. That misreading leads directly to a version written from memory, which is what REQ-VER-02 forbids.

traps.rule: Its version is recorded as unresolved in the manifest. B16 resolves it at H2.
traps.why: It was not read in the pass that produced the manifest. An unresolved entry is honest; a guessed one is not.

traps.rule: sha2 0.11 requires digest ^0.11. A dependency still pinning digest 0.10 puts two hasher generations in one binary; resolve it rather than allowing the duplicate.
traps.why: Verified from the crates.io index on 2026-09-22: sha2 0.11.0 declares digest ^0.11. The symptom is a duplicate-version finding in cargo-deny plus two incompatible Digest traits, so a hash computed by one generation cannot be verified by the other -- and REQ-UPD-02's artefact hash is exactly that comparison.
